text:
ConocoPhillips stock jumped 3.3% today to $141.22, driven by a sharp rise in crude oil prices following Saudi Arabia's closure of a major pipeline after a drone attack. U.S. oil climbed above $105 a barrel as the closure threatens to disrupt supplies, and analysts are warning that prices could spike further if the pipeline stays offline beyond a week—exactly the kind of supply squeeze that benefits large oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The stock is also riding a broader two-week rally, up 6.6% since early September as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have kept oil markets nervous. With the U.S. and world oil prices now $12 apart (suggesting some supply tightness), and with the Iranian foreign minister visiting China potentially signaling shifting alliances in the region, the market is pricing in sustained crude demand and higher energy prices ahead.
